sealedPropertiesCovered: graph is substrate not peer tool
question: C-2 — Is 'there are not four analysis products' right, or a category error?

accepted.detail: fit/graph/yagni as peer Tool universes force duplicate inventories and lateral deps. Graph-as-substrate and rules-over-facts are correct greenfield center.

partiallyRejected.claim: one analysis stage over profiles + one Probe stage is the full story
partiallyRejected.problem: Collapses two different architectural layers: (1) mechanism identity, (2) scheduling/stage identity. Differing cardinality, failure modes, and budgets are real — they belong to plan stages and profiles, not peer products.

distinctions.name: mechanism
distinctions.note: Same fact store, FactQuery, rule IR, fingerprint/Coverage model

distinctions.name: plan stages
distinctions.note: Index build is not 'just a query' in the scheduling sense — it is a materialization stage with its own cost, cache, and Coverage. Treating it only as presentation loses budget isolation.

distinctions.name: failure modes
examples: partial graph resolution vs rule policy fail vs advisory reduction confidence vs probe sandbox fail
distinctions.note: Same HostTermination union can express them; they must remain distinct reasonCodes / Coverage facets — not flattened into one 'analysis failed' UX

distinctions.name: user intent / presentation
distinctions.note: Profiles and projections — not separate engines

agent1Recommendation.sealCandidateWording: There is one analysis mechanism (facts, queries, rules, Coverage, Runs). There is not one flat analysis stage: the planner composes typed stages (extract, semantic, index, rule-packs, optional probe). Fitness, graph inspection, and reduction are profiles and projections over that mechanism — not peer products and not a single undifferentiated stage. Simulation remains a separate Probe contract.
agent1Recommendation.riskIfUnamended: Teams reintroduce graph-as-tool scheduling under a new name, or force all work into one budget pool and break agent-fast vs full-CI
